Bug_Title: XSS: Servlet reflected cross site scripting vulnerability in error page (XSS_REQUEST_PARAMETER_TO_SEND_ERROR)
Bug_Details:
This code directly writes an HTTP parameter to a Server error page (using HttpServletResponse.sendError). Echoing this untrusted input allows
for a reflected cross site scripting
vulnerability. See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-site_scripting
for more information. SpotBugs looks only for the most blatant, obvious cases of cross site scripting.
If SpotBugs found any, you almost certainly have more cross site scripting
vulnerabilities that SpotBugs doesn't report. If you are concerned about cross site scripting, you should seriously
consider using a commercial static analysis or pen-testing tool.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the doGet method where it directly writes the untrusted user input to a server error message. This allows for a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by passing a malicious script as a user input to the'showBug' method, which then gets reflected back to the client-side causing a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test code provided uses a user input that contains a script tag, which is a common trigger for cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. This input is passed to the showBug method of the XssBugServlet class, which in turn calls the doGet method with this input. The doGet method then throws an IOException with the user input included in the error message. This allows for the untrusted input to be reflected back to the user, creating a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability.
